data.name: Settings_General_LanguageHelp
data.value: Interface language. Changes apply immediately and are saved for future sessions.

data.name: Settings_General_SimbriefHelp
data.value: This is the username (alias) of your simbrief.com account, exactly as it appears in your profile. The app uses it to download your latest flight plan.

data.name: Custom_NotImplemented
data.value: Custom mode is not implemented yet. This feature will be available in a future version.

data.name: Train_Subtitle
data.value: Pick a scenario to practice emergency procedures.

data.name: Settings_BugHelp
data.value: Open an issue on GitHub describing what happened, what you were doing and what you expected to see.

data.name: Settings_BugTip
data.value: Tip: attach the most recent daily log and the individual report (crash-*.log), if any, along with the version you are using.

data.name: Settings_DonateText
data.value: If you enjoy Real Fenix Failures, you can support its development with a voluntary donation. It is a one-person independent project: nobody helps me; only the hobby and the wish for more realism in every flight keep me going. Every dollar helps move the project forward, gives me more drive to keep improving the app, and lets me put more resources into it. Thank you for being part of the project!

data.name: Settings_DownloadGoToReleases
data.value: Download and go to GitHub Releases

data.name: Settings_Help1Text
data.value: Start Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 with the Fenix A320 and wait until the cockpit is ready.

data.name: Settings_Help2Text
data.value: Realistic (failures based on your history), Training (preset scenarios) or Custom (manual control).

data.name: Settings_Help3Text
data.value: The app refreshes itself at all times: fly as usual and react to failures as in a real flight.

data.name: Settings_LogsHelp
data.value: Daily logs and individual error reports (crash-*.log / error-*.log) are in this folder.

data.name: Settings_PrivacyHelp
data.value: The ID is stored only on your computer (%AppData%\RealFenixFailures\userprefs.json) and is only used to query public SimBrief flight plans.

data.name: Settings_RealisticGraceHelp
data.value: When the app detects you landed and shut the engines down at the gate, it waits this many minutes before telling you that you can finish the session. Counted in real time, not simulator time. Allowed values: 0 to 999 (0 = notice immediately).

data.name: Settings_TelemetryHelp
data.value: Anonymous usage statistics: they help us improve the app with every release. They never include flight data or personal information. You can turn them off at any time.

data.name: Settings_UpdatesCheckHelp
data.value: The check queries the repository's public releases on GitHub. It also shows pre-releases, so you hear about test builds as soon as they ship.

data.name: Settings_UpdatesManualInstall
data.value: The app does not update itself: download the installer from GitHub Releases and replace the current version.

data.name: Rm_CompletionBanner
data.value: Flight completion detected (at gate, engines off). You can finish the session and view the summary.

data.name: Rm_FlightCompletedText
data.value: Flight completion detected: the aircraft landed and reached the gate with the engines off. Do you want to finish the realistic session and view the summary?

data.name: Rm_OfpUseridPrivacy
data.value: User ID stored only in your preferences (never in the database).

data.name: Rm_PauseTooltip
data.value: Pauses the failure engine: disarms active Fenix failures and blocks new ones until the session is resumed.

data.name: Rm_ProfileSelectorTooltip
data.value: Open the picker to choose the session's risk profile.

data.name: Rm_ReasoningFenixOffline
data.value: Fenix is not available: the session queues failures and sends them when Fenix comes back. Without Fenix, a failure is never armed on the aircraft.

data.name: Rm_ReasoningFuture
data.value: In the future this panel will show the engine's decision-level reasoning: why it picks or discards each failure. Until then, no events are simulated.

data.name: Rm_ReasoningNoData
data.value: No reasoning data yet: the decision backend does not exist yet, so there are no events to show.

data.name: Rm_ResumeTooltip
data.value: Resumes engine evaluation after a pause and re-arms in Fenix the failures that were in progress (best effort: failures that cannot be rebuilt stay in the log).

data.name: Rm_SessionFailuresDesc
data.value: Status: each failure is verified against Fenix's real state on every evaluation cycle: sent → confirmed active → resolved.

data.name: Rm_StartConfirmText
data.value: On VATSIM networks the ATC controller has the final say. If they order you to cancel your emergency, the pause that disarms failures is not implemented yet: use Stop and verify the disarm on the Fenix system. Finishing the session on the ground is preferred, but stopping in flight is allowed.

data.name: Rm_StopInFlightConfirm
data.value: ⚠ You are in flight (off ground). Stop the session now?

data.name: Rm_Subtitle
data.value: The system monitors your flight history and generates failures autonomously based on accumulated wear.

data.name: Rm_WearNoData

data.name: Rp_Low_Desc
data.value: Rare failures, almost always minor. For flying relaxed while you keep learning the aircraft.

data.name: Rp_Moderate_Desc
data.value: Occasional failures that can turn serious if the aircraft is worn. The balanced point.

data.name: Rp_High_Desc
data.value: Frequent and often severe failures, several at once. For those who handle emergencies with ease.

data.name: Rp_7700_Desc
data.value: Maximum pressure: chained severe failures with little respite. The "accident documentary" mode.

data.name: Rp_VatsimLowRest
data.value: you will almost never declare an emergency; you fly online with peace of mind.

data.name: Rp_VatsimModerateRest
data.value: the recommended online balance — real QRH work without forced diversions.

data.name: Rp_VatsimHighRest
data.value: you may have to divert or declare an emergency; let ATC know calmly.

data.name: Rp_Vatsim7700Rest
data.value: the emergency cadence is not manageable in frequency; meant for offline.
